content.text: A rigid steel cylinder of volume 0.012 m³ contains helium at a pressure of 1.5 × 10⁷ Pa and a temperature of 17 °C. Helium is a monatomic gas and is assumed to behave as an ideal gas.
Show that the amount of helium in the cylinder is about 75 mol.
Answer 75 mol is given; award the second mark only if 74.7 or the complete substitution is seen.
The cylinder is left in sunlight and the temperature of the helium rises to 46 °C.
Calculate the new pressure of the helium.
Allow use of PV = nRT with n = 75 mol (gives 1.66 × 10⁷ Pa).
Award [1 max] if Celsius temperatures are used (4.1 × 10⁷ Pa).
Explain, using the kinetic model of a gas, why the pressure of the helium increases.
the average speed / kinetic energy of the atoms increases
collisions with the walls are more frequent
the change in momentum in each collision is greater
Calculate the increase in the internal energy of the helium.
Suggest why the ideal gas model may
be accurate for the helium in this cylinder.
the pressure / density is high so the volume of the atoms is not negligible
compared with the volume of the cylinder
the atoms are close together so the forces between them are not negligible
Do not accept "helium is a real gas" without a reason.
